title: Moment, Torque & Conditions of Equilibrium
notes: The moment, or torque, of a force about a point is τ = r F sinθ. Here r is the distance from the point to the line of action, and θ is the angle between the position vector and the force. The perpendicular distance from the point to the line of the force is the moment arm.
A force through the pivot has zero moment arm, so it produces no torque about that pivot. That is why a hinge force can be removed from a torque equation by taking torques about the hinge.
Translational equilibrium means the body does not start to accelerate linearly. The vector sum of the forces is zero. In a plane this is two equations, one horizontal and one vertical.

Rotational equilibrium means the body does not start to rotate. The sum of the clockwise moments equals the sum of the anticlockwise moments about any point. Together with the force equations, this is the condition for complete equilibrium.
The sign of a torque is a choice. Clockwise negative and anticlockwise positive is a clear convention, as long as it is used for every force.
A light rod or beam is often taken to have no weight. If the beam is uniform, its weight acts at the midpoint. Leaving that weight out is a different problem from the one that was asked.

exercises.question: A light rod 2.0 m long is supported at its ends. A 40 N weight hangs 0.50 m from the left end. Find the two support forces.
steps: The rod is light, so it has no weight of its own.
Take torques about the left end. The left support has zero moment arm.
Clockwise moment of the weight is 40 × 0.50. Anticlockwise moment of the right support is N_right × 2.0.
N_right × 2.0 = 20, so N_right = 10 N. Then N_left = 30 N.
exercises.answer: Left support 30 N upward, right support 10 N upward.
